title: Late Renewal of Expired Rental Property Service Contracts
content:
An expired Rental Property Service Contracts contract that is renewed late, within its late-renewal grace period, takes a new term priced under the late-renewal premium basis, and the new-term premium is billed as one annual premium on the late renewal date. The basis applies to the premium of a late renewal only; every other premium charge remains under the premium billing terms.

## When the late-renewal premium is fixed

The late-renewal premium is fixed only after every tier upgrade made during the expired term carries its upgrade charge on the contract.

Put the other way round, in the same terms: while any tier upgrade made during the expired term does not yet carry its upgrade charge on the contract, the late-renewal premium is not fixed.

## What the late renewal does on the contract

The contract becomes active again for a new full term that starts on the late renewal date and ends the day ahead of the same calendar date the next year; the term number rises by one; the contract's end date and renewal notice date are cleared; the new term's annual premium is billed as one annual premium charge dated that day; and the premium balance rises by that premium.

## Invocation: `record_late_renewal_5b858282`

**Capability.** One call renews an expired rental property service contract late, within its grace period: it sets the contract back to active for a new full term that starts today and ends the day ahead of the same calendar date next year, raises the term number by one, clears the contract's end date and renewal notice date, bills the new term's annual premium as one annual premium charge dated today, and raises the premium balance by that premium. The landlord sees the contract active again with the new term dates and the annual premium on the billing history.

**How it is invoked.** An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `record_late_renewal_5b858282` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `landlord_contract_id` | the rental property service contract number of the expired contract, as returned by the rental contract lookup for the landlord | identifier text |
| `renewal_premium` | the annual premium for the new term | USD, a positive amount with 2 decimal places; stored rounded to 2 decimal places |
| `portfolio_discount_rate` | the portfolio discount rate the annual premium charge records | decimal fraction with 2 decimal places, for example 0.05; 0.00 when none |

**Return.** On success the receipt carries `status` "renewed"; `landlord_contract_id`; `contract_status` "active"; `term_start_date` and `term_end_date` of the new term as YYYY-MM-DD; `term_number` as an integer; `billing_entry_id`, the annual premium charge reference; `annual_premium` in USD with 2 decimal places; and `premium_balance`, the balance owed once the premium is billed, in USD with 2 decimal places.

*Hypothetical receipt:* a late renewal recorded on 12 July returns `contract_status` "active", a term from 12 July to 11 July of the next year, the term number raised by one and the annual premium shown on the billing history.
